penalties.authority: Office of the Deputy Commissioner, State Tax, Sector3, Noida, Uttar Pradesh
penalties.details: The Company has received a Show Cause Notice dated September 29, 2026 under Section 73 of the CGST Act, 2017, in connection to certain alleged discrepancies identified during scrutiny of the GST returns filed for FY 2022-23. This is a preliminary show cause notice and no order, demand or penalty has been confirmed. The Company was granted an opportunity to file a written reply substantiating full compliance with applicable GST laws and filing requirements. In response to the Show Cause Notice, the Company is examining the notice and will file a detailed reply with supporting documents within the prescribed time. Based on its preliminary assessment, the Company believes it has a good case on merits, and it does not expect any material impact on its financial position, operations or other activities. A personal hearing before the Proper Officer is scheduled for October 30, 2026, pursuant to which the Company will present its submissions and supporting documents.
penalties.impact: The notice proposes a potential financial liability of Rs. 5,39,39,622 comprising tax of Rs. 2,95,71,123, interest of Rs. 2,13,05,792 and penalty of Rs. 30,62,707. However, this is at the show cause stage only, is contested, and does not represent a confirmed liability. The Company intends to submit its reply along with relevant supporting documents and present its submissions before the Proper Officer at the scheduled personal hearing. The matter is not expected to have any material impact on the Company's financial, operational or other activities.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: An appellate order has been allowed in favour of ZNShine Solarworld Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Solarworld Energy Solutions Limited
tax_litigation.opposing_party: The Joint Commissioner (Appeal), State Tax, Uttarakhand, Dehradun
tax_litigation.status: The key findings and directions of the appellate order are as under: (a) The impugned order dated September 20, 2026 has been set aside; (b) The penalty of Rs. 1,22,12,498/- (being 200% of IGST of Rs. 61,06,249/-) imposed under Section 129 in respect of the imported consignment covered by Bill of Entry No. 3595328 dated September 05, 2026 and E-Way Bill No. 372332296102 dated September 12, 2026 has been annulled; (c) The goods have been held to be genuine imported goods duly covered by the Customs documents and Bill of Entry, and the failure to select the multi-vehicle option on the E-Way Bill portal while transporting the two containers through separate vehicles has been held to be a procedural/documentary lapse which does not establish tax evasion; (d) Any amount deposited by the Subsidiary pursuant to the impugned order (including Rs. 12,21,250/- deposited on September 21, 2026) shall be refunded/adjusted in accordance with law after verification; and (e) The vehicle and goods, if still under detention, shall be released forthwith, and the Proper Officer shall give consequential effect to the appellate order in the relevant records/portal. The details of the same were disclosed to the Stock Exchanges on September 23, 2026, pursuant to Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.
